atproto-iroh

Reference client. Functional, not precious — MIT-licensed on purpose; make it pretty if you want it prettier.

Identity

Persistent now: your did:iroh and every namespace this node has ever been granted into are loaded from disk on spawn — quitting and reopening the app doesn't lose either.

Your namespaces

    Members

    Every NodeProfile currently synced into a namespace — "who's here." Editing your own profile here overwrites your one fixed profile slot (safe: nobody else can write at your author's key); it doesn't create a new record each time.

      —

      Mute

      Purely local — no sync, no lexicon, changes nothing about what anyone else sees or whether a muted author's content keeps syncing (it does). Just filters what Messages shows you.

      —

        Share a namespace

        A ticket is a capability, not a link to a server — see SPEC.md §3.4/§3.6. Anyone holding it syncs this namespace directly with this node; nothing else grants or revokes it. Write is a shared secret with no per-holder revocation (SPEC.md §6 item 12) — everyone who ever holds it can write forever, but nobody can forge or overwrite anyone else's entries, so a Write ticket posted publicly is a real pattern, not a mistake: a public inbox, a dead drop, a graffiti wall anyone can add to. What it needs on the read side is moderation/volume handling, not restriction on the write side — see the Inbox section.

        Join a namespace

        Reads a ticket straight from a QR code via the device camera — the other half of "Show as QR" above. Decoding happens entirely on-device (a vendored jsQR, see dist/vendor/) — nothing about a scan is sent anywhere, it just fills in the field above. Needs camera access; if it's denied, or there's no camera (most desktops running this reference build), paste the ticket text instead.

        —

        Shared doc

        No schema, no lexicon — a document everyone with write access shares and edits, same sync and capability machinery as everything else here. "A Google doc without Google." Each save writes a new, immutable revision rather than overwriting the last one — two people editing the same doc while offline from each other both keep their edit. "Load" always refreshes the full history alongside it: if two revisions from different people landed close together in time, that's a real sign of a concurrent edit, and it's flagged rather than silently picking one. Click "Use this" on any revision to bring its text into the box below, review or merge by hand, then Save — that's how a conflict actually gets resolved here, not automatically.

        —

          Messages

          A namespace is the channel — no separate room concept. Each message gets its own auto-generated key (same collision-free pattern the Inbox below uses), so this needs no revision-history treatment the way Shared doc did: nobody's overwriting anybody else's message.

          —

            Tags

            One Tag type works across every record type, in any lexicon — tag a message, a Shared doc revision, anything with a subject ref. Click "Tag" next to a message above to fill the subject in below, or paste one manually ("{authorHex}/{collection}/{rkey}").

            —

              Images

              Uploaded as an ordinary namespace entry (`namespace::put_bytes`), not through a separate blob-fetch API — the same sync mechanism every other record here already relies on transfers the image bytes alongside their metadata. No thumbnailing; full images render inline.

              —

              Inbox

              Submit under a fresh, auto-generated key — no coordination needed between submitters, no collisions, nobody can overwrite anyone else's submission or the namespace owner's own records (SPEC.md §3.4's per-author identifier finding). Pair this with a Write QR code posted somewhere public and this is a public drop box, an anonymous tip line, a guestbook — whatever a "write-only-ish" namespace is good for. Read it back with the Inspector below, filtered to this prefix.

              —

              Polls

              A poll is a General-class governance Proposal, nothing more — same mechanism as everything in the full Governance section below, relabeled for the common case ("ask a question, let people weigh in") rather than a second thing built alongside it. Not a majority vote: it passes by default once voting closes unless enough people explicitly Object — silence counts as support. Use the full Governance section below for anything that needs Admit/Remove/Change-policy, an abstain/stand-aside signal, or a longer note on your vote.

              —

              Governance

              Objection-window ratification (SPEC.md §3.7.2/§3.9): a Proposal ratifies by default once its deadline passes unless enough block Signals land first. consent is recorded but carries no mechanical power. Eligibility and policy come from a real Founding claim posted at namespace creation (SPEC.md §6 item 16) — this app always founds a namespace as its sole genesis member; admitting anyone else goes through a real Proposal below.

              Inspector

              Every raw entry currently synced into a namespace — no per-record-type code, generic across whatever's in there (NodeProfile, a governance Proposal, anything added later). A debugging view, not a feature; see dump_all in namespace.rs.
